summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-09-29. Search budget ran out partway through the run. Only one fresh story met every rule: Stanford admitted that its dining office used AI to alter a student photo for campus ads, which broke the university's own AI policy (Inside Higher Ed and Fox News, both Sept. 23). Most of the ballot-error stories found were reported after the scan date, were already published or benched, lacked two accepted sources, or involved a party that isn't currently allowed. Genius: Scan for 2026-09-29 (genius). My search budget ran out early, so I worked mainly from the Space.com September archive and the official university pages linked from it. The strongest candidate is a UChicago-led JWST study, announced Sept. 23 in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, that found an atmosphere on HD 3167 b, the coldest lava world yet shown to have one. The second is a weaker alternate: a Yale-led simulation study, announced Sept. 23, on wandering black holes. The 2026 MacArthur Fellows (announced Sept. 29) are within the window, but I could not open an accepted news page for any fellow not already published. No genius story met the standard; nothing published.

candidates.headline: UChicago-led team finds an atmosphere on HD 3167 b, the coldest lava world known to have one
candidates.reason: Fails the 7-day freshness rule. The study ('Evidence for an Atmosphere on the Ultra-short-period Super-Earth HD 3167 b', Coy et al., ApJL 1005 L77) was published by The Astrophysical Journal Letters on 2026 July 9, according to the IOPscience article page in search results. A preprint (arXiv 2604.11911) was out in April 2026. The site's rules count journal publications from the day they were announced, and that is 82 days before the 2026-09-29 scan date. The UChicago News piece dated Sept 23 is a later promotional write-up of an old result (itself 'adapted from' an earlier Physical Sciences Division article), and the Space.com piece of Sept 29 just follows it. The proposed eventDate of 2026-09-23 misrepresents when the achievement happened.; Overstatement: the summary says the team 'used the James Webb Space Telescope to show that HD 3167 b ... has an atmosphere', and the headline says it 'finds an atmosphere' on 'the coldest lava world known to have one'. The paper's title and the university's own wording are more careful: 'evidence for an atmosphere', 'coldest lava world found so far with evidence of an atmosphere', and 'strong evidence'. Rewording could fix this, but it can't fix the date problem.; Minor: the summary says the day side 'is cooler than it would be without one'. The source says it is 'noticeably cooler than its expected maximum', which the researchers take as evidence of an atmosphere.

candidates.headline: Yale-led study finds galaxy mergers send black holes wandering for billions of years
candidates.reason: Too old for the 7-day window. The paper (Weller et al. 2026, ApJL 1008, L54, DOI 10.3847/2041-8213/ae9c38) was published on 2026-09-07. The IOPscience listing says 'Published 2026 September 7', and Space.com, the proposal's own source, says 'The team's research was published on Sept. 7 in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.' The scan date is 2026-09-29, so the window runs from Sept 23 to Sept 29. Our rules count journal publications from the day they are published, which makes this 22 days old. An arXiv preprint (2607.09853) and Astrobites coverage (Aug 11) also show the result was public before that.; The eventDate of 2026-09-23 is wrong. That is the date of Yale's own news release, not the date of the publication. A later university press release does not restart the clock on a three-week-old paper.; Minor: the headline says mergers 'send' black holes wandering for billions of years. This is a simulation result, and the sources say black holes 'can be displaced'. If it ran, it would need hedging ('can send', 'simulation suggests').
